metadata.title: Basketball Blaster: Every Feature, Played
metadata.audience: makers following the channel's Claude + Walker game workflows
metadata.note: godot-waikthrough walker film. Every gameplay beat is an exact-frame window of a scripted-input take of the real game; no human playtest. Game audio was not captured; narration only. No paid calls, no upload. Vertical companion: designed beats re-rendered as native 9:16 cards or 916 compositions; gameplay re-cut in portrait from the same frames.

beats.narration_text: Hola, this is Liam, in for Bear. Hand Walker a design document, and this is the kind of prompt it expects. This one is reconstructed, not a transcript. What came back is a playable Godot game, and this film plays every feature of it, with a script at the controls.

props.command: Please use Walker to convert my game design document about Basketball Blaster: Fowl Play — Mr. Block, armed with a basketball gun and basketball grenades, collects every egg across three arenas while chickens pour out of pipes — into a playable Godot project.
props.runningText: illustrative reconstruction — not the historical prompt
output: Built: 3 arenas, 8 scenes, 2,408 lines of GDScript.
Played here: 3 scripted-input takes, 76 of 76 assertions passing.

beats.narration_text: Basketball Blaster is an arena shooter. Mister Block fires basketballs at chickens across three arenas, and he wins by collecting eggs, not by racking up kills. Everything you'll see was played by a script, not a person.

props.text:
Basketball Blaster
is a basketball game.
Eggs win it, not kills.

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant writer: text is typed on screen over the narration, so mid-beat samples legitimately show a partial page. The finished text fills the safe area and holds for the last 1.5 s.

beats.narration_text: It opens on the title art with three buttons. How to Play lists every key, the controller layout, and seven rules: eggs clear an arena, grenades beep three times, three lives of three hits each. Back to Menu returns.

beats.narration_text: Play starts the pre-game briefing. The coach's first line types out letter by letter, and the prompt says enter or click to continue. So the script clicks the dialogue box. Nothing. It clicks above it. Still nothing: a full-screen shade layer eats every click. Enter works. A press mid-line finishes the line at once; the next press moves on. Eight lines later, Mister Block says let's ball, and the court fades in.

beats.narration_text: Arena one, Street Court. The banner says grab every egg. A walk, a jump, and a second Space in mid-air for the double jump. Shift fires the jetpack, and the blue bar is fuel. The gun tracks the crosshair, a ball every four tenths of a second, and right-click lobs the grenade. Two chickens tag him. Watch the health balls dim.

beats.narration_text: Now the script holds one spot and fights. With one health ball left, the next touch costs a life: a fade, and a respawn at the glowing gate. Then a grenade lands in a crowd, and four chickens go at once. Mega kill. Every death throws feathers and a splat that fades, and every hit shakes the camera. Ten kills later, the egg counter still reads one of five. Kills don't move it.

beats.narration_text: Arena three, the Fowl Play Finals: four pipes, a navy tint, seven eggs, and chickens that take four hits. This is the closest the run comes to losing. A life goes. Then another. Down to its last life, it keeps grabbing eggs. Seven of seven. Court cleared, one kill, one life left, and the button now reads Claim the Trophy.

beats.narration_text: F fires and G throws a grenade, for players without a mouse. On the controller, LB throws and RB burns the jetpack. The pause menu's Restart Arena reloads the court. Main Menu, and Quit closes the game.

beats.narration_text: Verdict. Everything implemented was played and seen working: three arenas, every move and weapon, pause, continue, defeat, retry, victory and quit. Two defects are on screen: the click that never continues, and HUD hints drawn over their own bars. And one design question: rushing eggs beats fighting. Whether any of it is fun is a person's call. Nobody has played it yet.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude in your own Godot project: Use Walker on my Godot game. Write an input-only capture script that plays one feature through real key and mouse events, asserts what should happen on screen, and fails loudly if it doesn't. Then tell me one thing the capture can't prove. That last part matters: a script that wins is not a player who had fun. Liam, in for Bear.
